news.title: FIFA blames UEFA for 'smear campaign' against Infantino
news.lede: The dispute between the two football associations reached a US court, in which UEFA is looking for permission to collect evidence for criminal proceedings in Switzerland. World football governing body FIFA took a lash at Europe's UEFA for starting a "smear campaign" and "fishing expedition" against FIFA and its President Gianni Infantino. This comes after a dispute between the two organizations due to FIFA's plan to sell a stake in its commercial rights, with UEFA submitting an ex parte application to the US District Court in New York to obtain testimony and documents from US-based entities. These documents will be used in potential criminal proceedings in Switzerland, where both FIFA and UEFA are based.

news.title: Thomas Tuchel undergoes secret England World Cup inquest as FA prepare huge report on tactics and squad selection
news.lede: ENGLAND chief Thomas Tuchel’s World Cup tactics came under the microscope during a secret inquest at St George’s Park last week. The Three Lions notched their best performance in the tournament since 1966 by bagging bronze. But Tuchel, 53, came under fire when England threw away their lead and suffered a last-gasp semi-final defeat to Argentina after going defensive. And the former Chelsea boss headed to St George’s Park to reflect on the summer extravaganza.

news.title: Thomas Tuchel's intensive World Cup inquest as FA prepare major report into England failings
news.lede: The FA have carried out an inquest with England manager Thomas Tuchel to assess exactly what went wrong in the Three Lions' agonising World Cup semi-final loss to Argentina. On paper, the summer competition in the USA, Mexico and Canada was the country's second-best showing in the competition. The 6-4 win over France in the third-place play-off meant Tuchel, technically, led England to their greatest campaign since the 1966 triumph. However, it felt anything but jubilant, due to the Three Lions allowing a 1-0 lead to slip through their hands before losing to two quick-fire goals against the Argentinians.
